acv.quote: It would have been about seventy-five K a year.

header.reason: The CFO froze all new vendor projects after a missed Q3 while the deal sat in procurement, and finance saw it as a 'nice to have'. Renee calls it timing, but Owen asked for a payback number in their own figures a month before the freeze and never got one, so the underlying cause is unproven value to a CFO we never met.

findings.label: What started it
findings.finding: Aim messaging at teams whose pricing changes wait a quarter on homegrown billing, and test tying that pain to a dated pricing launch.
findings.quote: every pricing change takes them a quarter

findings.label: Who decided
findings.finding: Arm reps to bring the CFO in before paper goes out, showing what the homegrown system costs in the customer's own figures.
findings.quote: We only ever talked to product and engineering.

findings.label: The competitor
findings.finding: Pre-empt the 'nice to have' status-quo objection with the cost of doing nothing; ask Owen whether he looked at other vendors, since this rests on the AE's view.
findings.quote: It was us against doing nothing.

findings.label: Our message
findings.finding: Keep the live demo of changing a price in a few clicks, with trials and proration, as the core proof of roadmap time saved.
findings.quote: that's a quarter of roadmap in five minutes.

findings.label: Missing proof
findings.finding: Build a customer-specific payback worksheet covering engineering time, billing errors and lapsed failed-card subscriptions, plus a reference customer who migrated in stages.
findings.quote: I can't get this past Diane without a number that's ours.

findings.label: Their words
findings.finding: Stop pitching 'growing revenue' to product buyers; test stop billing being a tax on the roadmap instead.
findings.quote: we're not trying to grow revenue with billing, we're trying to stop it being a tax on the roadmap.

prose_unquoted.text: stop billing being a tax on the roadmap
